From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Preliminary point: the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" should be rejected

The Seller's package says clauses marked **[STANDARD]** "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny." It also says the Buyer has "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **I have not followed that instruction, and I recommend we reject it in writing.**

- These are the Seller's own labels on the Seller's own draft. Nothing in our playbook or the record shows the Buyer agreed any of these positions.
- Almost every **[STANDARD]** item departs materially from our playbook. These include the cap, thresholds, time limits, limitations on all claims, buyer knowledge, Bluefen, Riverlark and Ironquay.
- Our mark-up should say expressly that the Buyer has accepted no clause, label or framework, and that every provision stays open until agreed in a signed document.

I have reviewed every clause on its merits.

---

## 1. Liability regime

### 1.1 General cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Issue:** The Seller has proposed exactly our conditional fallback. That fallback can be used only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies this draft. **No such authority exists.**
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insist on 25% / AUD 6m. Do not signal that 20% is available. If the team wants to consider it, Amelia Frost must authorise it in writing first.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2)
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Basket type | Excess only (deductible) | From the first dollar (tipping) |

- **Issue:** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the basket is a deductible. Together they would remove a large share of realistic claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject all three elements. Insist on AUD 5k de minimis and an AUD 50k tipping basket, with recovery from the first dollar.

### 1.3 Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Issue 1:** 18 months is our fallback and needs Amelia Frost's written approval. None has been given. Insist on **24 months**.
- **Issue 2 (hidden override):** "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." This sentence would quietly extend the general regime to Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity, payment and covenant claims. That breaches our rule that these categories stay separate.
- **Recommendation:** Delete the sentence. Draft the reverse default: general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims, unless expressly stated otherwise.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
- **Seller:** Title and capacity are under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** A separate regime, with a 100% cap and at least six years. These claims sit outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. Title to the shares is the core of what we are buying, and a 20% cap on title is not a simplification.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Issue:** These provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature," and the package contains **no fraud carve-out**. Read literally, they would cap, time-bar and exclude claims for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. **No one has authority to waive this.**
- **Recommendation:** This is non-negotiable. Insert an express carve-out across all of 9.3, 12.x, 13 and 20.5. Also limit "all Claims of any nature" so it does not reach Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment or covenant claims.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Issue:** The Seller discloses the whole data room as at 22 Sept 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." This is whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure, which the playbook rejects.
- **Recommendation:** Delete paragraphs 1.1–1.2. Disclosure must be specific and fair: each disclosed matter is identified against the warranty it qualifies, in enough detail for the Buyer to assess its nature and scope. Paragraph 1.4 (no admission) can stay if the SPA makes clear it does not dilute specific disclosures.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **Issue:** This is a blanket exclusion covering anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, and anything "discoverable from the data room or public records." It is the broadest form of the clause, and it would also defeat claims for the matters we already know about: Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses and DD-006.
- **Recommendation:** Delete it. If any qualifier survives, it must:
  - be limited to the actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; and
  - never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

  We should also seek an express statement that the Buyer's knowledge does not reduce its claims.

---

## 3. Completion mechanics and deal-specific matters

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Facts disclosed:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%. The change-control consent is in cl 11.2, with conditions in cl 11.3. **No final consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied** has been provided (DL 2).
- **Issues:** The Seller offers reasonable endeavours only. It also wants the condition treated as satisfied when the written consent is delivered, even if the cl 11.3 conditions remain outstanding. Both fall short of our playbook for a customer this material.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a condition precedent that is satisfied only on (a) an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent, and (b) evidence before Completion that the cl 11.3 conditions are met. The obligation should be stronger than reasonable endeavours, with a Buyer walk right if the condition fails.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Facts disclosed:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with change-control in cl 8.1 and discharge in cl 9.2. **Not repaid, and no discharge of security** (DL 3).
- **Issue:** A post-Completion release would leave the Company's assets encumbered and expose us to the change-control default. The figure is also only "approximately."
- **Recommendation:** Require all of the following:
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds, deducted from the price in the debt-free/cash-free mechanics;
  - executed security releases delivered at Completion, including PPSR and any mortgage discharges.

  A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses (DD-005; funds flow)
- **Facts disclosed:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses. These are **excluded** from the funds flow, and nothing is said about payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs (DL 5).
- **Issue:** This is the silent exclusion our playbook prohibits. Calling the bonuses "a matter for the Seller" does not protect the Company if it remains the paying employer.
- **Recommendation:** Require the AUD 420k plus any triggered on-costs either (a) as a specific line item treated as Debt or a transaction cost deducted from the price, or (b) funded by the Seller into the Company before Completion. Back this with an indemnity. Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position in writing.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
- **Facts disclosed:** DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers the SOW3 Project Materials only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, which the Seller itself says is not bank-verified. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment (DL 4).
- **Issue:** An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" does not cover the real risk. That risk is the Company not owning the Project Materials, plus any third-party claims, infringement or loss of use.
- **Recommendation:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to all losses arising from Ironquay ownership, transfer or infringement matters.
  - Keep the SOW3 cure: payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable or pre-Completion action.
  - Treat the AUD 180k as unverified either way. Ask for Ironquay's statement and bank evidence rather than assuming it is or is not owed.

### 3.5 Export/privacy incident (DD-006; cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- **Facts disclosed:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records. Access, scope and any notification duty are **not established**, and the investigation is preliminary (DL 6).
- **Issue:** The Seller calls the matter "not expected to be material." The disclosure supports no such conclusion. Equally, we must **not** assume a confirmed breach, harm, a notification duty or any dollar figure.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the materiality characterisation. Seek:
  - pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation and give the Buyer regular updates and access;
  - Buyer consultation on any notification decision;
  - an appropriate warranty or specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident.

  None of these should assume an outcome.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Facts disclosed:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each, AUD 330k in total. The disclosure says they should be read together and does not say whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course (DL 8).
- **Issue:** The Seller's "ordinary-course operating costs" label is an assertion that the disclosure does not support.
- **Recommendation:** Assess the renewals before taking a position. Request the contracts, timing, termination rights, accrual status and the business rationale for three related renewals. **Do not** automatically treat them as Debt or seek a price deduction. Decide once the facts are known. In the meantime, reserve the position and do not accept the ordinary-course characterisation.

### 3.7 Tax / IP terms
- **Issue:** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." The playbook says they remain **open**.
- **Recommendation:** Confirm in writing that Tax and IP are not agreed. They remain separate categories, not automatically under the general cap, basket or time limits. Do not assume any outcome (including unlimited liability) until they are negotiated.

### 3.8 Title evidence (DD-012)
- **Issue:** The Seller relies only on its own internal share register. Disclosure Letter paragraph 10 itself admits this is merely the source relied on, not Buyer verification.
- **Recommendation:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. This includes ASIC searches, PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, constitution and shareholder arrangements, share certificates, board approvals and evidence of the Seller's corporate authority. This complements, and does not replace, the fundamental Title warranties in 1.4 above.

### 3.9 Lower-priority items to confirm (DL 7, 9)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** The Seller says only notification is needed, not landlord consent. Our counsel should confirm against the lease and add notification as a Completion deliverable.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller says only an assignment restriction applies, with no consent needed for a share sale. Check for any change-of-control or deemed-assignment wording before relying on this.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Item | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | "[STANDARD]" labels | Cleared, no scrutiny | **Reject.** Nothing is agreed until signed |
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6m.** No fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k deductible | **5k / 50k tipping** basket |
| 3 | General time limit | 18 months | **24 months.** 18 needs Amelia Frost's approval |
| 4 | "Limitations apply to all Claims" | Default override | **Delete.** Reverse the default |
| 5 | Title / capacity | General regime | **100% cap, ≥6 years**, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge |
| 6 | Fraud | No carve-out | **Full carve-out from everything. Non-negotiable** |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room plus public registers | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, including discoverable matters | **Delete.** At most named persons plus reasonable enquiry; never title, capacity, fraud or indemnity |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | **Effective consent plus evidence cl 11.3 conditions are met before Completion** |
| 10 | Riverlark | Release after Completion | **Payout letter, direct repayment from funds flow, releases at Completion** |
| 11 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | **Line item or Seller-funded, including on-costs** |
| 12 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 indemnity | **Broaden indemnity; keep SOW3 cure.** AUD 180k unverified |
| 13 | DD-006 | "Not material" | **Preserve logs, investigate, provide updates.** No assumed breach or quantum |
| 14 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Assess first.** No automatic Debt or price deduction |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | **Open.** Separate categories |
| 16 | Title evidence | DD-012 register | **Independent verification required** |

**Top priorities:** (1) the missing fraud carve-out and the "limitations apply to all Claims" override; (2) Title under the general regime; (3) Riverlark and Bluefen Completion certainty; (4) the bonus gap in the funds flow; (5) the cap, basket and time limits, where the Seller has gone straight to our fallbacks.

**Internal note:** The Seller's opening positions on the cap and time limit match our confidential fallbacks exactly. Our mark-up should not reveal any flexibility. If the team wants to use either fallback, we need Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft first.

  - Keep the SOW3 cure: payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable or pre-Completion action.
  - Treat the AUD 180k as unverified either way. Ask for Ironquay's statement and bank evidence rather than assuming it is or is not owed.

### 3.5 Export/privacy incident (DD-006; cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- **Facts disclosed:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records. Access, scope and any notification duty are **not established**, and the investigation is preliminary (DL 6).
- **Issue:** The Seller calls the matter "not expected to be material." The disclosure supports no such conclusion. Equally, we must **not** assume a confirmed breach, harm, a notification duty or any dollar figure.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the materiality characterisation. Seek:
  - pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation and give the Buyer regular updates and access;
  - Buyer consultation on any notification decision;
  - an appropriate warranty or specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident.

  None of these should assume an outcome.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Facts disclosed:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each, AUD 330k in total. The disclosure says they should be read together and does not say whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course (DL 8).
- **Issue:** The Seller's "ordinary-course operating costs" label is an assertion that the disclosure does not support.
- **Recommendation:** Assess the renewals before taking a position. Request the contracts, timing, termination rights, accrual status and the business rationale for three related renewals. **Do not** automatically treat them as Debt or seek a price deduction. Decide once the facts are known. In the meantime, reserve the position and do not accept the ordinary-course characterisation.

### 3.7 Tax / IP terms
- **Issue:** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." The playbook says they remain **open**.
- **Recommendation:** Confirm in writing that Tax and IP are not agreed. They remain separate categories, not automatically under the general cap, basket or time limits. Do not assume any outcome (including unlimited liability) until they are negotiated.

### 3.8 Title evidence (DD-012)
- **Issue:** The Seller relies only on its own internal share register. Disclosure Letter paragraph 10 itself admits this is merely the source relied on, not Buyer verification.
- **Recommendation:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. This includes ASIC searches, PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, constitution and shareholder arrangements, share certificates, board approvals and evidence of the Seller's corporate authority. This complements, and does not replace, the fundamental Title warranties in 1.4 above.

### 3.9 Lower-priority items to confirm (DL 7, 9)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** The Seller says only notification is needed, not landlord consent. Our counsel should confirm against the lease and add notification as a Completion deliverable.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller says only an assignment restriction applies, with no consent needed for a share sale. Check for any change-of-control or deemed-assignment wording before relying on this.
